sanskrit: ājñāpya tu mahārājo rāghavasyābhiṣecanam priyārhāṃ priyam ākhyātuṃ viveśāntaḥpuraṃ vaśī
english: Having ordered the consecration of Rāghava, the great king — self-controlled and desirous of bearing glad tidings to one who deserved gladness — entered the inner apartments.

sanskrit: tāṃ tatra patitāṃ bhūmau śayānām atathocitām pratapta iva duḥkhena so 'paśyaj jagatīpatiḥ
english: There the lord of the earth saw her fallen to the floor, lying prostrate in a manner wholly unbecoming her — he, who was himself as though scorched with grief.

sanskrit: sa vṛddhas taruṇīṃ bhāryāṃ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasīm apāpaḥ pāpasaṃkalpāṃ dadarśa dharaṇītale
english: That aged king — himself without guilt — beheld upon the ground his young wife, dearer to him than life itself, yet harbouring wicked intent.

sanskrit: kareṇum iva digdhena viddhāṃ mṛgayuṇā vane mahāgaja ivāraṇye snehāt parimamarśa tām
english: As a great elephant in the forest tenderly touches a she-elephant pierced by a hunter's poisoned arrow, so did he, in affection, stroke her.

sanskrit: parimṛśya ca pāṇibhyām abhisaṃtrastacetanaḥ kāmī kamalapatrākṣīm uvāca vanitām idam
english: Having touched her with his hands, his heart greatly alarmed, the passion-bound king spoke thus to the lotus-eyed woman.

sanskrit: na te 'ham abhijānāmi krodham ātmani saṃśritam devi kenābhiyuktāsi kena vāsi vimānitā
english: "I do not perceive what anger has taken hold in your heart, O queen. By whom have you been aggrieved? By whom have you been dishonoured?"

sanskrit: yad idaṃ mama duḥkhāya śeṣe kalyāṇi pāṃsuṣu bhūmau śeṣe kimarthaṃ tvaṃ mayi kalyāṇa cetasi bhūtopahatacitteva mama cittapramāthinī
english: "O auspicious one, why do you lie thus in the dust for my grief? Why do you lie upon the ground, tormenting my heart — you whose heart is auspicious — as though possessed by an evil spirit?"

sanskrit: santi me kuśalā vaidyā abhituṣṭāś ca sarvaśaḥ sukhitāṃ tvāṃ kariṣyanti vyādhim ācakṣva bhāmini
english: "I have skilled physicians, all of them entirely devoted. They shall bring you comfort — tell me your ailment, O lovely one."

sanskrit: kasya vā te priyaṃ kāryaṃ kena vā vipriyaṃ kṛtam kaḥ priyaṃ labhatām adya ko vā sumahad apriyam
english: "Whose favour shall I do for you? Who has done you displeasure? Who shall today receive great benefit, or who shall receive great harm?"

sanskrit: avadhyo vadhyatāṃ ko vā vadhyaḥ ko vā vimucyatām daridraḥ ko bhavatv āḍhyo dravyavān vāpy akiṃcanaḥ
english: "Shall one who is not to be slain be slain, or shall one condemned to death be freed? Shall a poor man be made wealthy, or a wealthy man be stripped of all?"

sanskrit: ahaṃ caiva madīyāś ca sarve tava vaśānugāḥ na te kaṃ cid abhiprāyaṃ vyāhantum aham utsahe
english: "I myself and all that is mine are under your command. I dare not thwart any purpose of yours."

sanskrit: ātmano jīvitenāpi brūhi yan manasecchasi yāvad āvartate cakraṃ tāvatī me vasuṃdharā
english: "Speak, even at the cost of my own life, whatever your heart desires — the entire earth over which the wheel of sovereignty turns is mine."

sanskrit: tathoktā sā samāśvastā vaktukāmā tad apriyam paripīḍayituṃ bhūyo bhartāram upacakrame
english: Thus reassured, she, intending to speak that which was hateful, set about further tormenting her husband.

sanskrit: nāsmi viprakṛtā deva kena cin na vimānitā abhiprāyas tu me kaś cit tam icchāmi tvayā kṛtam
english: "I have not been wronged by anyone, O lord, nor dishonoured. But there is a certain desire of mine — I wish it to be fulfilled by you."

sanskrit: pratijñāṃ pratijānīṣva yadi tvaṃ kartum icchasi atha tad vyāhariṣyāmi yad abhiprārthitaṃ mayā
english: "Make me a promise — swear that you will do it — and then I shall speak what it is that I desire."

sanskrit: evam uktas tayā rājā priyayā strīvaśaṃ gataḥ tām uvāca mahātejāḥ kaikeyīm īṣadutsmitaḥ
english: Thus spoken to by his beloved, the king — fallen under a woman's sway — replied to Kaikeyī with a slight smile, the great-spirited one.

sanskrit: avalipte na jānāsi tvattaḥ priyataro mama manujo manujavyāghrād rāmād anyo na vidyate
english: "O proud one, do you not know — there is no person dearer to me than you, save that tiger among men, Rāma?"

sanskrit: bhadre hṛdayam apy etad anumṛśśyoddharasva me etat samīkṣya kaikeyi brūhi yat sādhu manyase
english: "O gentle one, search even this heart of mine and draw it forth — having considered this, Kaikeyī, say what you think right."

sanskrit: balam ātmani paśyantī na māṃ śaṅkitum arhasi kariṣyāmi tava prītiṃ sukṛtenāpi te śape
english: "Knowing your own power, you ought not to be doubtful of me. I will bring you joy — I swear to you by my good deeds."

sanskrit: tena vākyena saṃhṛṣṭā tam abhiprāyam ātmanaḥ vyājahāra mahāghoram abhyāgatam ivāntakam
english: Elated by those words, she disclosed her inner intention — dreadful as Death himself approaching.

sanskrit: yathākrameṇa śapasi varaṃ mama dadāsi ca tac chṛṇvantu trayastriṃśad devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ
english: "As you swear in due order and grant me the boon — let the thirty-three gods headed by Indra hear that!"

sanskrit: candrādityau nabhaś caiva grahā rātryahanī diśaḥ jagac ca pṛthivī caiva sagandharvā sarākṣasā
english: "Let the moon and sun, the sky and planets, night and day and the directions, the whole world and the earth itself, along with Gandharvas and Rākṣasas —"

sanskrit: niśācarāṇi bhūtāni gṛheṣu gṛhadevatāḥ yāni cānyāni bhūtāni jānīyur bhāṣitaṃ tava
english: "— the night-roaming creatures, the household deities dwelling in houses, and whatever other beings there are — let them all know your spoken word."

sanskrit: satyasaṃdho mahātejā dharmajñaḥ susamāhitaḥ varaṃ mama dadāty eṣa tan me śṛṇvantu devatāḥ
english: "This great-splendoured one, true to his word, knowing dharma, and well-composed — he grants me a boon. Let the gods hear this for me."

sanskrit: iti devī maheṣvāsaṃ parigṛhyābhiśasya ca tataḥ param uvācedaṃ varadaṃ kāmamohitam
english: Thus the queen, having embraced and adjured the great archer, then spoke further to that boon-granting one bewildered by desire.

sanskrit: varau yau me tvayā deva tadā dattau mahīpate tau tāvad aham adyaiva vakṣyāmi śṛṇu me vacaḥ
english: "The two boons that were given to me by you at that time, O lord of the earth — I shall now state them this very day. Listen to my words."

sanskrit: abhiṣeka samārambho rāghavasyopakalpitaḥ anenaivābhiṣekeṇa bharato me 'bhiṣicyatām
english: "The consecration that has been prepared for Rāghava — with this very consecration let my Bharata be anointed."

sanskrit: nava pañca ca varṣāṇi daṇḍakāraṇyam āśritaḥ cīrājinajaṭādhārī rāmo bhavatu tāpasaḥ
english: "And let Rāma, wearing bark garments, deerskin, and matted locks, dwell as an ascetic in the Daṇḍaka forest for nine and five years."

sanskrit: bharato bhajatām adya yauvarājyam akaṇṭakam adya caiva hi paśyeyaṃ prayāntaṃ rāghavaṃ vane
english: "Let Bharata today assume the undisputed rank of crown prince — and this very day let me see Rāghava setting out for the forest."

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutvā mahārājaḥ kaikeyyā dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ vyathito viklavaś caiva vyāghrīṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā mṛgaḥ
english: Then the great king, having heard Kaikeyī's terrible words, was distressed and agitated, like a deer that has seen a tigress.

sanskrit: asaṃvṛtāyām āsīno jagatyāṃ dīrgham ucchvasan aho dhig iti sāmarṣo vācam uktvā narādhipaḥ moham āpedivān bhūyaḥ śokopahatacetanaḥ
english: Seated upon the uncovered ground, breathing long and deep, crying out "Alas! Shame!" in anguish, the lord of men fell once more into a swoon, his consciousness overwhelmed by grief.

sanskrit: cireṇa tu nṛpaḥ saṃjñāṃ pratilabhya suduḥkhitaḥ kaikeyīm abravīt kruddhaḥ pradahann iva cakṣuṣā
english: After a long while the king regained his senses, deeply distressed; in fury he spoke to Kaikeyī, as though burning her with his gaze.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃse duṣṭacāritre kulasyāsya vināśini kiṃ kṛtaṃ tava rāmeṇa pāpe pāpaṃ mayāpi vā
english: "O cruel one, O evil in conduct, O destroyer of this family — what wrong has Rāma done you, O sinful woman? What wrong have I done you?"

sanskrit: sadā te jananī tulyāṃ vṛttiṃ vahati rāghavaḥ tasyaiva tvam anarthāya kiṃnimittam ihodyatā
english: "Rāghava always behaves toward you as he would toward his own mother — for what reason are you roused to work his ruin?"

sanskrit: tvaṃ mayātmavināśāya bhavanaṃ svaṃ praveśitā avijñānān nṛpasutā vyālī tīkṣṇaviṣā yathā
english: "You were brought by me into my own house for my own destruction — a princess, not properly known, like a venomous serpent."

sanskrit: jīvaloko yadā sarvo rāmasyeha guṇastavam aparādhaṃ kam uddiśya tyakṣyāmīṣṭam ahaṃ sutam
english: "When all the living world here sings the praises of Rāma's virtues, pointing to what offence shall I abandon my beloved son?"

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ vā sumitrāṃ vā tyajeyam api vā śriyam jīvitaṃ vātmano rāmaṃ na tv eva pitṛvatsalam
english: "I could abandon Kausalyā, or Sumitrā, or royal fortune, or even my own life — but never Rāma, who is devoted to his father."

sanskrit: parā bhavati me prītir dṛṣṭvā tanayam agrajam apaśyatas tu me rāmaṃ naṣṭā bhavati cetanā
english: "My joy is supreme when I behold my eldest son; but when I do not see Rāma, consciousness itself forsakes me."

sanskrit: tiṣṭhel loko vinā sūryaṃ sasyaṃ vā salilaṃ vinā na tu rāmaṃ vinā dehe tiṣṭhet tu mama jīvitam
english: "The world might endure without the sun, or crops without water — but my life could not remain in this body without Rāma."

sanskrit: tad alaṃ tyajyatām eṣa niścayaḥ pāpaniścaye api te caraṇau mūrdhnā spṛśāmy eṣa prasīda me
english: "Therefore, abandon this resolve, O you who are resolved on sin. With my head I touch your feet — be gracious to me."

sanskrit: sa bhūmipālo vilapann anāthavat striyā gṛhīto dṛhaye 'timātratā papāta devyāś caraṇau prasāritāv ubhāv asaṃspṛśya yathāturas tathā
english: That lord of the earth, lamenting like one helpless, seized by the woman in her exceeding firmness, fell — and, like one sick, could not quite reach the two extended feet of the queen.

sanskrit: atadarhaṃ mahārājaṃ śayānam atathocitām yayātim iva puṇyānte devalokāt paricyutam
english: That great king — lying prostrate in a manner wholly unbefitting him, like Yayāti fallen from the world of the gods at the exhaustion of his merit —

sanskrit: anartharūpā siddhārthā abhītā bhayadarśinī punar ākārayām āsa tam eva varam aṅganā
english: — that woman, herself the embodiment of calamity yet successful in her purpose, fearless though she showed fear, demanded once again that very same boon.

sanskrit: tvaṃ katthase mahārāja satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ mama cemaṃ varaṃ kasmād vidhārayitum icchasi
english: "You boast, O great king, of being truthful and firm in your vow — why then do you wish to withhold this boon of mine?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kaikeyyā rājā daśarathas tadā pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtaṃ vihvalann iva
english: Thus addressed by Kaikeyī, King Daśaratha replied in anger, reeling for a moment as though bewildered.

sanskrit: mṛte mayi gate rāme vanaṃ manujapuṃgave hantānārye mamāmitre rāmaḥ pravrājito vanam
english: "When I am dead and Rāma — that foremost of men — has gone to the forest: alas, O ignoble woman, O my enemy, Rāma has been banished to the forest!"

sanskrit: yadi satyaṃ bravīmy etat tad asatyaṃ bhaviṣyati akīrtir atulā loke dhruvaṃ paribhavaś ca me
english: "If I speak truly in this, then may it be untrue — for surely boundless infamy and dishonour will be mine in this world."

sanskrit: tathā vilapatas tasya paribhramitacetasaḥ astam abhyagamat sūryo rajanī cābhyavartata
english: As he lamented thus, his mind whirling in confusion, the sun set and night drew on.

sanskrit: sa triyāmā tathārtasya candramaṇḍalamaṇḍitā rājño vilapamānasya na vyabhāsata śarvarī
english: That night of three watches, adorned by the orb of the moon, did not shine beautifully for the king as he lamented in such affliction.

sanskrit: tathaivoṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya vṛddho daśaratho nṛpaḥ vilalāpārtavad duḥkhaṃ gaganāsaktalocanaḥ
english: So too the aged king Daśaratha, breathing hot sighs, lamented his sorrow like one in anguish, his eyes fixed upon the sky.

sanskrit: na prabhātaṃ tvayecchāmi mayāyaṃ racito 'ñjaliḥ atha vā gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ nāham icchāmi nirghṛṇām nṛśaṃsāṃ kaikeyīṃ draṣṭuṃ yatkṛte vyasanaṃ mahat
english: "I do not wish for a dawn to come through you — this folded salutation I now make. Or rather, go away quickly — I do not wish to see the merciless and cruel Kaikeyī, on whose account this great calamity has befallen."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājā kaikeyīṃ saṃyatāñjaliḥ prasādayām āsa punaḥ kaikeyīṃ cedam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus, the king then, with hands folded in supplication, sought once more to propitiate Kaikeyī, and spoke to her again.

sanskrit: sādhuvṛttasya dīnasya tvadgatasya gatāyuṣaḥ prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ devi bhadre rājño viśeṣataḥ
english: "Let grace be shown — especially to this king of upright conduct, now wretched, dependent upon you, and with life nearly spent. O queen, O gentle one."

sanskrit: śūnyena khalu suśroṇi mayedaṃ samudāhṛtam kuru sādhu prasādaṃ me bāle sahṛdayā hy asi
english: "This was spoken by me in utter desolation, O lovely-hipped one. Show me proper grace — you are, after all, a woman of feeling."

sanskrit: viśuddhabhāvasya hi duṣṭabhāvā tāmrekṣaṇasyāśrukalasya rājñaḥ śrutvā vicitraṃ karuṇaṃ vilāpaṃ bhartur nṛśaṃsā na cakāra vākyam
english: Yet she who harboured a wicked heart, though he was pure of heart — she, merciless, made no reply to her husband even after hearing that wondrous and piteous lamentation of the king, whose eyes were red and brimming with tears.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā punar eva mūrchitaḥ priyām atuṣṭāṃ pratikūlabhāṣiṇīm samīkṣya putrasya vivāsanaṃ prati kṣitau visaṃjño nipapāta duḥkhitaḥ
english: Then the king, looking once more upon his beloved who was unsatisfied and speaking contrary words regarding the banishment of his son, fell insensible to the ground, stricken with grief.

sanskrit: putraśokārditaṃ pāpā visaṃjñaṃ patitaṃ bhuvi viveṣṭamānam udīkṣya saikṣvākam idam abravīt
english: That sinful woman, gazing upon the descendant of Ikṣvāku — tormented by grief for his son, fallen unconscious to the ground and writhing — spoke thus.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kṛtveva kim idaṃ mama saṃśrutya saṃśravam śeṣe kṣititale sannaḥ sthityāṃ sthātuṃ tvam arhasi
english: "As though having committed a sin, why do you lie collapsed on the floor after having heard my promise? You ought to stand firm in your resolve."

sanskrit: āhuḥ satyaṃ hi paramaṃ dharmaṃ dharmavido janāḥ satyam āśritya hi mayā tvaṃ ca dharmaṃ pracoditaḥ
english: "Those who know dharma declare that truth is the highest dharma. Relying on truth, I have urged you toward dharma as well."

sanskrit: saṃśrutya śaibyaḥ śyenāya svāṃ tanuṃ jagatīpatiḥ pradāya pakṣiṇo rājañ jagāma gatim uttamām
english: "Śaibya the lord of the earth, O king, having pledged and then given his own body to the hawk, attained the highest destiny."

sanskrit: tatha hy alarkas tejasvī brāhmaṇe vedapārage yācamāne svake netre uddhṛtyāvimanā dadau
english: "Similarly the splendid Alarka, when a brahmin learned in the Vedas begged of him, plucked out his own eyes and gave them without hesitation."

sanskrit: saritāṃ tu patiḥ svalpāṃ maryādāṃ satyam anvitaḥ satyānurodhāt samaye velāṃ khāṃ nātivartate
english: "The lord of rivers, bound to truth, does not, by its truth-compact, transgress the appointed shoreline at the proper season, however narrow that boundary."

sanskrit: samayaṃ ca mamāryemaṃ yadi tvaṃ na kariṣyasi agratas te parityaktā parityakṣyāmi jīvitam
english: "And if you will not honour this noble compact of mine, then, before your very eyes, having been abandoned, I shall abandon my life."

sanskrit: evaṃ pracodito rājā kaikeyyā nirviśaṅkayā nāśakat pāśam unmoktuṃ balir indrakṛtaṃ yathā
english: Thus pressed by the fearless Kaikeyī, the king was unable to free himself from the snare — like Bali from the bond fashioned by Indra.

sanskrit: udbhrāntahṛdayaś cāpi vivarṇavanado 'bhavat sa dhuryo vai parispandan yugacakrāntaraṃ yathā
english: Bewildered in his heart, he became pale and voiceless — like a draught-ox struggling between the yoke and the wheel.

sanskrit: vihvalābhyāṃ ca netrābhyām apaśyann iva bhūmipaḥ kṛcchrād dhairyeṇa saṃstabhya kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: The lord of the earth, his eyes unsteady and as though unseeing, summoning his composure with great difficulty through his fortitude, spoke thus to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: yas te mantrakṛtaḥ pāṇir agnau pāpe mayā dhṛtaḥ taṃ tyajāmi svajaṃ caiva tava putraṃ saha tvayā
english: "The hand of yours which I clasped in fire at the sacred rite, O sinful woman — that I renounce, and your son who is my own kin, and you along with him."

sanskrit: tataḥ pāpasamācārā kaikeyī pārthivaṃ punaḥ uvāca paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ vākyajñā roṣamūrchitā
english: Then Kaikeyī — wicked in her conduct, yet skilled in speech — overcome with rage, spoke harsh words to the king once more.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ bhāṣase rājan vākyaṃ gararujopamam ānāyayitum akliṣṭaṃ putraṃ rāmam ihārhasi
english: "What is this you say, O king — words like a poison's sting? You should have Rāma, your son, brought here without delay."

sanskrit: sthāpya rājye mama sutaṃ kṛtvā rāmaṃ vanecaram niḥsapatnāṃ ca māṃ kṛtvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi
english: "Having established my son in the kingdom, having sent Rāma to dwell in the forest, and having left me without a rival — you will then be one whose purpose is accomplished."

sanskrit: sa nunna iva tīkṣeṇa pratodena hayottamaḥ rājā pradocito 'bhīkṣṇaṃ kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Goaded repeatedly like a noble horse urged by a sharp goad, the king spoke thus to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: dharmabandhena baddho 'smi naṣṭā ca mama cetanā jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ priyaṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi dhārmikam
english: "I am bound by the bond of dharma and my understanding has forsaken me. I wish to see Rāma, my beloved eldest son, that righteous one."

sanskrit: iti rājño vacaḥ śrutvā kaikeyī tadanantaram svayam evābravīt sūtaṃ gaccha tvaṃ rāmam ānaya
english: Hearing the king's words, Kaikeyī thereupon herself spoke to the charioteer: "Go, bring Rāma here."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā taṃ sūtaṃ sannaharṣaḥ sutaṃ prati śokāraktekṣaṇaḥ śrīmān udvīkṣyovāca dhārmikaḥ
english: Then that majestic and righteous king, his joy extinguished in regard to his son, his eyes red with grief, looked up at the charioteer and spoke.

sanskrit: sumantraḥ karuṇaṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā dīnaṃ ca pārthivam pragṛhītāñjaliḥ kiṃ cit tasmād deśād apākraman
english: Sumantra, having heard the piteous words and seen the wretched state of the king, withdrew a little from that spot with hands folded in reverence.

sanskrit: yadā vaktuṃ svayaṃ dainyān na śaśāka mahīpatiḥ tadā sumantraṃ mantrajñā kaikeyī pratyuvāca ha
english: When the lord of the earth was unable out of misery to speak himself, then Kaikeyī — well-versed in counsel — spoke to Sumantra.

sanskrit: sumantra rāmaṃ drakṣyāmi śīghram ānaya sundaram sa manyamānaḥ kalyāṇaṃ hṛdayena nananda ca
english: "Sumantra, I wish to see Rāma — bring the handsome one quickly." He, thinking this to be auspicious, rejoiced in his heart.

sanskrit: sumantraś cintayām āsa tvaritaṃ coditas tayā vyaktaṃ rāmo 'bhiṣekārtham ihāyāsyati dharmavit
english: Sumantra reflected, hastened on by her: "Clearly Rāma, who knows dharma, will come here for the consecration."

sanskrit: iti sūto matiṃ kṛtvā harṣeṇa mahatā punaḥ nirjagāma mahātejā rāghavasya didṛkṣayā
english: Having so resolved, the charioteer of great splendour went forth once more, with great joy, eager to behold Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ purastāt sahasā vinirgato mahīpatīn dvāragatān vilokayan dadarśa paurān vividhān mahādhanān upasthitān dvāram upetya viṣṭhitān
english: Then, having gone forth suddenly from the front, looking about at those standing at the gateway of the lords of the earth, he saw various townspeople of great wealth who had come and stood assembled at the door.
